text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Clinton says China will be more democratic over time and American engagement policy can help encourage change.
- Iraq's President Saddam Hussein puts his wife under house arrest after shooting of his son in December.
- Singapore welcomes 7.500 Japanese women coming on incentive tour.
- Resale flats in new Housing Development Board estates enjoy faster valuation growth.
- Six newcomers to Singapore stock exchange account for about a third of total volume on main and second boards in past eight trading days.
- Singapore Telecom and Singapore Technologies join forces with 11 other top telecommunications comapanies in region to develop multimedia applications and services.
- Jade Technologies surprises with 40 percent gain on first trading day.
- U.S. dollar soars by more than two yen in Tokyo trading to reach 122.75 yen, highest level since February 1993.
- Lum Chang subsidiary LC Development is going into wine business with Jendami Pty Ltd to buy Chittering Estate Winery for Australia $2.15 million.
- Sapura Holdings Bhd aborts bid to acquire 30 percent stake in UMW Holdings Bhd.
- Hong kong electronics manufacturer and distributor IDT International says it will gain over Hong Kong $63 million from recent spinoff of its LCD arm, IDT Holdings (Singapore).
- Jumabhoy holding company Scotts Investment tells Singapore High Court of losses of Singapore $50 million.
- Creative Technology hits 16-month high of Singapore $17.90 on expectations of good results.
